items.name: Fiji (ImageJ)
items.blurb: The reference image-analysis platform for biology — ImageJ bundled with hundreds of curated plugins for segmentation, registration, tracking and stitching.

items.name: PyMOL (Open Source)
items.blurb: The molecular graphics system behind a large share of published structure figures, in its community-maintained open-source build.

items.name: UCSF ChimeraX
items.blurb: Molecular visualisation built for large structures, cryo-EM maps and publication-quality renders, from the team behind Chimera.

items.name: Ketcher
items.blurb: Browser-based chemical structure sketcher for drawing molecules and reactions, with SMILES and MOL import and export.

items.name: pLannotate
items.blurb: Annotates engineered plasmids automatically — paste a sequence and get back labelled features, ready to check or export.

items.name: Cytoscape
items.blurb: The standard desktop platform for building, styling and analysing biological networks, extended by a large app store.

items.name: RStudio Desktop
items.blurb: The open-source IDE for R — the working environment for most Bioconductor and tidyverse analysis.

items.name: SuperPlotsOfData
items.blurb: Turns replicate-level data into SuperPlots in the browser, showing every point and the independent experiments behind the summary statistics.

items.name: Visual Studio Code
items.blurb: General-purpose editor that has become the default for analysis scripts and notebooks, with first-class Python and R support.

items.name: Zotero
items.blurb: Reference manager that collects papers from the browser, syncs a library and inserts citations into Word, LibreOffice and Google Docs.

items.name: Obsidian
items.blurb: Plain-text notes stored as local Markdown files, with backlinks and graph views — a lab notebook you keep, in a format that outlives the app.
